title: Principles one to five
hookLine: God exists, is one, has no body, is eternal, and alone is to be worshiped

cards: One what? It's a question a child might ask, and Maimonides takes it seriously.

Behind it stands a line from Deuteronomy that Jewish prayer comes back to morning and night: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." His list builds on it, and takes up the child's questions one by one.
One like a single apple is one? One like a team is one? And if the Torah talks about God's hand and God's eyes, does God have hands and eyes?
His first five foundations are his answers. Today, the stretch of the list about God.

teach.h: GOD EXISTS, AND ALL ELSE LEANS ON GOD.
teach.b: Principles one to five. The first: God exists, and everything else exists because of God. Not the other way around.
The world leans on God; God doesn't lean on the world. The second: God is one. And here Maimonides is careful.
Not one like one of a pair, and not one like one member of a kind. Not one like a single body, which can still be cut into parts.
A oneness, he says, unlike any other oneness.
The third: God has no body. So what about the hand of God, the eyes of the LORD? He reads them as the Torah speaking in human language, so that people can understand.
Deuteronomy reminds Israel that at Sinai they heard a voice but saw no form at all.
The fourth: God is eternal. Before everything, after everything. In Isaiah's words: "I am the first, and I am the last."
The fifth: only God is to be worshiped. Not the stars, not angels, not any power in between, as if God needed a go-between. Prayer goes straight to God.
Now put them side by side. Each one takes something away. God isn't caused.
God isn't many. God isn't a body. God doesn't begin or end.
God doesn't need a messenger. Maimonides teaches God, here, mostly by saying what God is not.

how: Jews say the Shema, "Hear, O Israel," in the morning and evening prayers and at bedtime; Maimonides' first principles are often taught alongside it, and his explanations of them are studied in his commentary and in the opening chapters of the Mishneh Torah.

games.q: what does “principles one to five” mean?
o: five commandments about how to pray each day
the first foundations: God exists, is one, has no body
the five books of the Torah, listed by name

games.q: principles one to five — tap the pairs.
p: God exists; all else leans on God

s: Maimonides reads "the hand of God" as a real hand
he reads it as the Torah speaking in human language, so people can understand.
for Maimonides, God's oneness is like one of a pair
he says it is a oneness unlike any other: not one of a pair or of a kind.
the fifth principle says worship goes to God alone
not to stars, angels or any power in between.

games.q: you're reading the Torah and it mentions the hand of God. you're Maimonides. how do you read it?
o: God has a hand, like ours.
the Torah speaks in human language, so people can understand.
the verse must be a copying mistake.
games.why: he holds that God has no body, and reads such phrases as the Torah speaking in human language.

practice: Let the word one arrive on the in-breath, and let it go on the out-breath. When a picture comes with it, a number, a shape, a face, let it pass; Maimonides kept taking pictures away.
If you pray, you can say the line from Deuteronomy once, quietly.

wordCard.voice: Principles one to five. The first stretch of Maimonides' list: God exists, is one, has no body, is eternal, and alone is to be worshiped. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: one, the last word of the line "Hear, O Israel."

carryVoice: Your line: one, bodiless, eternal. No picture is big enough, so he kept setting them down. See you tomorrow.
